Welcome to LibrePaper. Edit this sentence in the browser and watch the draft
update. Your Quarto source, comments, highlights, and checkpoints travel with
the document.

## Source and preview

This file is Quarto. Markdown preview renders a fast, execution-free draft in the browser. Quarto preview asks the local companion to run your installed Quarto, R or Python and displays that local result. The server synchronizes shared source and assets; it neither executes the code cell nor uploads the live preview.

## A small scientific example

For a sample of size $n$, the standard error of a mean is

$$
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

A formula is a rule a machine can be made to follow, the point Ada Lovelace
made when she described the Analytical Engine weaving algebraic patterns
[@lovelace1843]. Type `@` in the editor to cite another entry from
`references.bib`.

{{< include sections/rendering.qmd >}}

The icon in @fig-librepaper is a relative project asset. Change the values in
the cell below, render locally, and make a checkpoint for the new result.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "A small summary computed by Quarto."
values <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
data.frame(statistic = c("Mean", "Sample size"),
           value = c(mean(values), length(values)))
```

## What Quarto adds

Quarto combines Markdown prose with executable R or Python cells, captions, and
cross-references. The browser can show a saved result while collaborators edit
the source. Try changing `values` and leave a comment on this paragraph.

## Working with other clients

Use `librepaper sync` to keep a local editor synchronized, or bind the companion to a project folder whose private inputs remain on your computer. Publishing a finished HTML file creates an HTML document that readers can open without R, Python, or Quarto.
